steps.title: The two present tenses
steps.html:
Present SimplePresent Continuous
Use it forwhat is always true, or a habitwhat is happening now, or this week
Formwork / worksam / is / are working
Negativedon't / doesn't workam not / isn't / aren't working
QuestionDo / Does you work?Are you working?
Signal wordsevery day, usually, often, nevernow, at the moment, today, this week

Ask yourself: is this true in general, or is it happening at this moment?

State verbs — know, like, want, need, have (= own) — stay in the Present Simple.

The most useful sentence at this level is: I usually…, but today I'm…

steps.title: Look at the pairs.

She normally works in the office, but this week she's working at home.
They play tennis on Thursdays, but they aren't playing today.
He doesn't drink coffee, but he's drinking one right now.
I know the answer. — not I'm knowing.
